section_4b_pre_print_debates.debate_title: Debate 1: Retail Trading Take-Rate Compression vs. Institutional ETF Custody Scale
section_4b_pre_print_debates.bull_vs_bear_framing: Bulls argue that Coinbase retains an unrivaled brand moat with retail take rates holding firm (~1.4% blended consumer fee) while institutional custody fees expand rapidly as Coinbase custodies >80% of all US spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETF assets. Bears counter that spot ETF fee competition and low-cost international platforms will inevitably exert downward pressure on retail transaction fees, eroding high-margin consumer trading revenue.
section_4b_pre_print_debates.call_focus_question: Analyst Conference Call Focus: Are retail trading take rates showing any sign of deterioration following the launch of options on spot crypto ETFs, and what is the effective fee rate earned on institutional custody assets?

section_4b_pre_print_debates.debate_title: Debate 2: Stablecoin Yield Resilience in a Federal Reserve Easing Cycle
section_4b_pre_print_debates.bull_vs_bear_framing: Bulls point out that USDC circulating market cap has surged over +35% in 2026, more than offsetting 50–75 bps of Fed rate cuts via volumetric expansion and international remittance adoption. Bears warn that every 100 bps reduction in Fed funds rates reduces Coinbase's annual pre-tax income by ~$140M unless circulating USDC supply accelerates at an unsustainable pace.
section_4b_pre_print_debates.call_focus_question: Analyst Conference Call Focus: What is Coinbase's sensitivity model for stablecoin revenue per 25 bps Fed rate cut, and how much incremental yield is generated from global non-USDC fiat balances?

section_4b_pre_print_debates.debate_title: Debate 3: Base Layer-2 Monetization & Regulatory Clarity Catalyst
section_4b_pre_print_debates.bull_vs_bear_framing: Bulls believe Coinbase's Layer-2 network Base is becoming the default execution environment for onchain finance, stablecoin payments, and consumer social apps, while evolving US crypto legislative clarity (FIT21 / market structure) removes the SEC litigation discount. Bears caution that regulatory settlement costs and Layer-2 fee compression from competing rollups could constrain long-term Base monetization.
section_4b_pre_print_debates.call_focus_question: Analyst Conference Call Focus: What timeline does management foresee for formal legislative market structure enactment, and what are the primary revenue drivers for Base over the next 12–18 months?
